query: Who was the president of the Sinn Fein political party during the Hume-Adams Dialogue?

pipeline_result.response: The president of the Sinn Féin political party during the Hume-Adams Dialogue was Éamon de Valera, who served as the head of government and head of state. He also led the introduction of the Constitution of Ireland.
retrieved_context: Hume–Adams dialogue: The Hume–Adams dialogue was a series of talks between then Social Democratic and Labour Party leader John Hume and Sinn Féin leader Gerry Adams during the Northern Ireland peace process.

Leader of Sinn Féin: The leader of Sinn Féin (alternatively known as the "Uachtarán Shinn Féin" or "President of Sinn Féin") is the most senior politician within the Sinn Féin political party in Ireland.  Since 13 November 1983, the office has been held by Gerry Adams, following the resignation of Ruairí Ó Brádaigh as leader of the party.

Éamon de Valera: Éamon de Valera ( ; ] ; first registered as George de Valero; changed some time before 1901 to Edward de Valera; 14 October 1882 – 29 August 1975) was a prominent politician and statesman in 20th-century Ireland.  His political career spanned over half a century, from 1917 to 1973; he served several terms as head of government and head of state.  He also led the introduction of the Constitution of Ireland.
